headline: Showers taper off by Saturday; a Freeze Watch covers parts of southwest Washington, then a dry, mild stretch into midweek.
summary: A cool, slightly unstable low-pressure system off the coast is drifting slowly south, bringing showers to western Washington this afternoon, some with moderate rain. Forecasters gave a slight chance of thunderstorms through this afternoon. Mountain snow levels were forecast around 3000 to 3500 feet with light precipitation, so only small new snow amounts are expected. Temperatures fall through Saturday morning. A Freeze Watch is in effect from late Friday night through Saturday morning for the lowlands of Lewis and southern Thurston counties, where lows are forecast in the upper 20s to around 32 degrees, cold enough to kill crops and sensitive plants. Forecasters say the middle Chehalis River valley may also need a freeze alert, since lows there are approaching the upper 20s, but that is less certain. The low weakens and moves inland south of the area on Saturday, and conditions start to dry out. Saturday should be partly sunny and dry, with highs in the mid 50s and no rain expected for festivities around the region. High pressure aloft builds from Sunday into the middle of the week. A few weak systems may pass through, but they are unlikely to bring more than extra clouds, and any rain would not be significant. Highs stay in the mid 50s. Forecasters say Nov 6 through 12 could turn wetter, but that is only a possibility and they will keep evaluating it.
changes: The morning discussions focused on showers fading to the coast and only mentioned lows in the mid 30s to lower 40s. By midday, forecasters added a Freeze Watch for Lewis and southern Thurston county lowlands, said a Chehalis valley freeze alert may be needed, and made Saturday sound drier and partly sunny. They also noted a possibly wetter Nov 6 through 12.
